27209.description:
Retail Supervisor
Coastal Retail Services Limited is seeking a reliable, customer-focused, and experienced
Retail Supervisor
to oversee daily retail store operations and lead our retail team in delivering excellent customer service, proper stock control, and strong sales performance.
The successful candidate will be responsible for supervising staff, managing store operations, monitoring inventory, ensuring accurate cash handling, maintaining store presentation, and supporting the achievement of sales targets.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Supervising daily store opening, closing, and retail operations.
Leading and monitoring cashiers, sales assistants and other retail staffs.
Ensuring excellent customer service and handling customer complaints professionally.
Monitoring sales performance and supporting the achievement of sales targets.
Ensuring proper product display, pricing, tagging, merchandising, and store cleanliness.
Checking stock levels, assisting with stock receiving, and supporting regular stock counts.
Monitoring damaged, expired, missing, or slow-moving stock.
Ensuring accurate cash handling, sales recording, EFTPOS transactions, and daily sales reconciliation.
Maintaining compliance with company policies, internal controls, safety standards, and security procedures.
Preparing and submitting daily sales, stock movement, staff attendance, and operational reports.
REQUIREMENTS:
Grade 12 certificate or equivalent.
Certificate or Diploma in Business, Retail Management, Sales, Accounting, or a related field is an advantage.
At least
2–3 years’ experience
in retail operations, sales, or customer service environment.
Previous supervisory experience is preferred.
Good leadership and staff supervision skills.
Strong customer service and communication skills.
Basic knowledge of cash handling, sales reconciliation, inventory, and stock control.
Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and POS systems.
Ability to work under pressure, including weekends, public holidays, and extended hours when required.
Honest, reliable, disciplined, and trustworthy character.
Key Competencies
The ideal candidate should be:
Customer-focused and service-oriented.
Organized and detail oriented.
Firm but fair in supervising staff.
Able to lead by example.
Proactive in solving operational issues.
Committed to store cleanliness, safety, sales performance, and loss prevention.
Interested applicant should send their cover letter, updated Resume and other supporting documents to this email:
[email protected]
or

th

27080.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
A
bout us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Responsible for operating different types of Heavy Equipment in a safe and appropriate manner to carry out earth moving tasks as directed by the shift supervisor for general mining operations.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Safely operate different types of Heavy Equipment as part of underground mining work plan pre task jobs.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Responsible for loading and transporting ore or ore waste.
Ensure the equipment is delivered for service when scheduled.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must obtain a minimum qualification of Grade 10 or above with experience in operating Front-End loaders Volvo L90G and L90H or similar models and must have 2+ years’ experience in operating different types of equipment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Possess current Class 7 driver’s license.
Must have operating certificate.
Ability to work with close supervision.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

24579.description:
PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.
CHARTER MANAGER
We are pleased to announce an open vacancy exists in our Commercial Department for a qualified and experienced
Charter Manager
.
Based in Port Moresby, this position will report to the GM Commercial according to the specific description outlined below.
OVERALL DESCRIPTION
The Charter Manager is responsible for developing the Charter Market and managing delivery of products/services into that space. The position is responsible for building Adhoc and long-term charter contracts within both the Government and resource sectors.
Maintain and oversee existing contracts, ensuring all obligations are met.
Ensure compliance with aviation regulations, service level agreements (SLAs), and safety standards.
Conduct contract reviews and risk assessments, identifying safety and operational risks.
Manage and participate in contractor audits to ensure compliance with safety and performance standards.
Provide detailed contract performance reports to the CEO and senior management.
Assess contract profitability, risks, and operational efficiency for continuous improvement.
Ensure contract renewals, amendments, and modifications are aligned with company objectives.
Conduct research on PNG’s charter aviation market, identifying trends and opportunities.
Provide insights to senior leadership on potential new markets, competitors, and pricing strategies.
Analyze market conditions to develop new charter offerings and business strategies.
Optimize opportunities for regular and hoc charter services
Most importantly targets are met.
Identify and pursue new contracts and partnership opportunities to grow the charter business.
Develop customized charter solutions for corporate and government clients.
Negotiate and secure new business agreements with organizations needing charter services.
Oversee the service delivery process for all charter clients, ensuring operations meet contractual obligations.
Ensure smooth execution of charter flight schedules, ground handling, and logistics.
Address and resolve service-related issues to maintain client satisfaction and contract integrity.
Work with flight operations, ground services, and maintenance teams to ensure service reliability.
Ensure compliance with aviation safety, operational efficiency, and performance metrics.
Monitor aircraft availability and scheduling to meet contractual obligations.
Develop and maintain regular charter performance reports, tracking key operational indicators.
Implement measures to improve on-time performance, reduce cancellations, and enhance efficiency.
Provide feedback to operations and management teams on service improvements and optimizations.
QUALIFICATION/EXPERIENCE
Tertiary qualities preferably in Business and or Finance related discipline
Experience in the Aviation industry treated favorably
PNG or emerging market economies experience is an advantage
Experience in managing contracts
5 – 10 years of industry experience
If you feel you meet our requirements and are interested, we would like to hear from you. Send your application in only one PDF file to:
[email protected]
Applications close:
Friday 26
th
June 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
We are an equal opportunity employer.
Apply

27370.description:
We are seeking a competent and flexible individual to fill the vacant position of
Earthworks & Road Maintenance Manager
. This position is based in
Kimbe, West New Britain Province
and reports to the Head of Operations – West New Britain.
EARTHWORKS & ROAD MAINTENANCE MANAGER
Job Purpose:
The Earthworks & Road Maintenance Manager is responsible for planning, directing, and overseeing all activities related to earthmoving operations and the maintenance of road infrastructure. The core purpose of this role is to ensure that roads and associated civil works are constructed, maintained, and repaired efficiently, safely, and to required standards, supporting reliable transportation and operational continuity.
Main Responsibilities:
Ensure that all earthworks and road maintenance activities are carefully planned, sequenced, and executed within defined timelines to avoid delays and disruptions.
Planning and allocating site earthwork crews, machinery, and haul trucks to meet strict deadlines.
Ensuring Road design dimensions (camber, slopes, and elevations) accurately match engineering plans.
Develop, enforce, and continuously improve QA/QC procedures in line with project specifications, engineering standards, and regulatory requirements.
Identify defects or non-conformances, implement corrective actions, and ensure proper documentation and reporting of quality performance across all maintenance activities.
Conducting Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) and managing risk around open excavations and heavy traffic zones.
Enforce adherence to occupational health and safety (OHS) standards, company policies, and legal requirements across all earthworks and road maintenance activities.
Prepare and manage budgets for earthworks and road maintenance projects, ensuring efficient allocation of resources (labour, materials, equipment).
Monitoring fuel consumption, tracking material yields, managing sub-contractor billings, and reporting daily progress to stakeholders.
Monitor actual expenditure against budget, identify cost variances, and implement cost-control measures to keep projects financially on track.
Compile regular reports on project costs, resource utilization, progress, and financial performance for management review.
Job Requirements:
Degree or Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.
5 to 10+ years of hands-on experience in heavy civil construction, specifically focusing on earthmoving, cut-and-fill operations, grading, and road paving.
At least 3 to 5 years in a supervisory or management role managing subcontractors, surveyors, and heavy machinery operators.
Proficiency in interpreting civil road design blueprints, grading plans, cross-sections, and surveying benchmarks.
Deep understanding of soil mechanics, compaction levels, moisture density testing, and material selection (e.g., aggregates, asphalt, concrete).
Practical knowledge of heavy machinery operation and production capacities (e.g., excavators, bulldozers, graders, compactors, and scrapers).
Knowledge of stormwater management, sub-grade drainage, culvert installation, and trenching compliance.
Familiarity with project scheduling software (e.g., Primavera P6, MS Project), CAD viewers, and GPS-guided grading systems (like Trimble or Topcon).
Ability to work in outdoor, high-noise environments exposed to extreme weather conditions, dust, and heavy machinery vibration.
Strong physical stamina to navigate uneven terrain, climb into machinery, and perform regular site walkthroughs.
Interested applicants can submit an application consisting of a cover letter, updated C.V and supporting documents to the address below.
New Britain Palm Oil Ltd, Human Resources Office
Private Mail Bag, Kimbe – WNB
Applications close –
Wednesday, 24th June 2026
To Apply

[email protected]
.  Please include the Job ID "
#27370
" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.

27211.description:
Lead a strong, established general insurer in a growing Pacific market
Deliver profitable growth with disciplined underwriting and reinsurance strength
Drive strategic expansion, capability uplift, and stronger market relationships
THE ORGANISATION
We are partnering with a leading general insurer operating in Papua New Guinea who is seeking a high-calibre Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organisation into its next phase of disciplined growth, capability uplift, and strategic expansion.
This is a rare opportunity to take the helm of a well-established underwriting-focused insurer with strong market positioning, deep broker relationships, and a reputation for financial discipline in a complex and highly relationship-driven market.
The business is entering a period of strategic development, with a focus on sustainable growth, portfolio optimisation, and selective expansion into adjacent insurance segments, supported by strong reinsurance capacity and governance frameworks.
THE OPPORTUNITY
This is a full CEO mandate with complete accountability for organisational performance, strategic execution, and stakeholder engagement. You will lead a respected insurer operating in a broker-influenced market where underwriting discipline, relationship strength, and technical credibility are critical to success.
The role requires a leader who is hands on, is a mentor with a knowledge sharing approach who can balance commercial growth ambitions with strong risk governance and long-term portfolio sustainability.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Provide end-to-end leadership of the organisation across all functions
Deliver sustainable, profitable growth aligned to Board direction
Maintain strong underwriting discipline and portfolio integrity
Oversee reinsurance strategy, placement, and partner relationships
Strengthen broker, client, and stakeholder relationships across the market
Lead financial performance, capital discipline, and operational efficiency
Build and develop a high-performing leadership team and culture
Support selective expansion into new product areas and market segments
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
Success in this role will be defined by:
Consistent profitable growth with disciplined underwriting outcomes
Strong retention and strengthening of the core insurance portfolio
Improved broker and reinsurer confidence and engagement
Expansion into selected growth segments
Enhanced organisational capability and leadership depth
Stable, well-governed, and high-performing business platform
CANDIDATE PROFILE
We are seeking a senior insurance executive with 15–20+ years of industry experience, ideally at CEO, COO, GM, or senior underwriting leadership level.
You will bring:
Strong technical grounding across property, casualty, liability, and related lines
Proven underwriting and/or claims leadership capability
Demonstrated experience in reinsurance programme management
Strong commercial acumen with full P&L accountability
Experience operating in broker-driven insurance environments
Background in emerging, regional, or complex markets highly regarded
Exposure to medical insurance, digital distribution, or insurance technology will be an advantage.
LEADERSHIP CAPABILITY
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Strong executive presence and Board-level credibility
Ability to influence and manage diverse stakeholders
Commercial discipline with a long-term strategic mindset
Cultural adaptability in less structured market environments
High integrity and strong governance orientation
A leadership style that balances technical authority with relationship focus
LOCATION
This is a resident-based leadership role located in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. The successful candidate must be willing to be fully based in-country and engage actively with the local market.
REMUNERATION
A highly competitive executive package will be offered, including:
Market-aligned base salary
Performance-based incentive structure
Housing and education support
Executive benefits including vehicle and medical cover
Relocation support where applicable
This is a confidential executive search. Interested candidates should submit a detailed CV outlining relevant experience and achievements.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Apply

27426.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
The Team Leader – Fleet is responsible for leading the Fleet Management function by overseeing all fleet operations, maintenance planning, vendor coordination, and compliance requirements. The role ensures that all vehicles are safe, well-maintained, legally compliant, and available to support business operations. This includes leading fleet staff, managing vendor relationships, maintaining fleet asset records, and continuously improving fleet processes to support operational efficiency.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Develop and manage preventative fleet maintenance schedules.
Prioritise work programs to meet operational and safety objectives.
Coordinate structured fleet meetings with team members, vendors, and internal stakeholders.
Identify short- and long-term fleet management priorities.
Review and update fleet plans, maintenance cycles, and asset replacement schedules.
Communicate fleet requirements clearly with internal teams, drivers, and external service providers.
Present complex information in clear, simple language.
Facilitate effective communication channels between fleet operations and other departments.
Resolve conflicts or disagreements constructively.
Use electronic communication tools appropriately.
Lead positive customer service culture within Fleet Management.
Manage relationships with repair workshops, leasing partners, suppliers, and safety equipment installers.
Oversee GPS and dash cam installation, tracking, and maintenance.
Conduct regular inspections of vendor work quality and report on performance.
Prepare weekly reports on all fleet-related vendor activities.
Supervise and support Fleet Officers and Drivers.
Train, coach, and mentor staff in best-practice fleet management and safety standards.
Identify staff strengths and development needs.
Promote continuous improvement and professional development.
Set performance objectives and monitor results for fleet personnel.
Conduct regular inspections of vehicles and ensure safety or compliance issues are addressed immediately.
Monitor registration, safety stickers, NAC passes, and all compliance deadlines.
Ensure Pre-start Checklists are properly completed before maintenance or repair tasks.
Maintain accurate inventory of spare parts, tyres, lubricants, and other maintenance essentials.
Monitor fuel consumption and maintain detailed records.
Oversee the maintenance of fleet databases, logs, and documentation.
Assist with procurement, replacement, and disposal of fleet vehicles.
Prepare monthly fleet condition and performance reports.
Maintain driver records, including licenses and vehicle user agreements.
Support continuous process improvement initiatives in fleet management.
Perform other duties as required by Manager or Head of Department.
Promote and uphold safety standards within the fleet team.
Conduct and document regular vehicle safety inspections.
Identify and mitigate potential fleet-related hazards.
Encourage continuous improvement of OHS practices in fleet operations.
Ensure drivers and fleet officers comply with all safety protocols.
REQUIREMENTS
Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Management, Logistics, or a related discipline.
Certificate in Fleet Management, Automotive Technology, or Project Management (highly desirable).
Relevant technical training or certification in vehicle operations/maintenance is an advantage.
Minimum 5 years' experience in fleet management or transport operations.
Demonstrated experience leading a team and managing vendor relationships.
Strong knowledge of PNG statutory requirements for compliance, registration, and safety.
Proven experience managing complex fleet operations, reporting, and scheduling.
Experience in training, coaching, or developing staff.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Ability to manage fleet budgets and control operational costs.
Effective leadership and supervision skills.
Strong prioritisation and organisational ability.
Good communication, report-writing, and interpersonal skills.
High ethical standards and professionalism.
Ability to remain calm and solutions-focused in a dynamic environment.
Competence in conflict resolution.
HOW TO APPLY;
If you are passionate about pursuing a career with Moni Plus and enjoy being part of a high-performing support team, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience and why you are the ideal candidate for this position. Please address your application to
Head of Human Capital
, Moni Plus, PO Box 1748, Boroko, NCD via email
[email protected]
and apply now. Please note only shortlisted applicants will be contacted to proceed. Applications close
Tuesday, 23
rd
June 2026.
We offer competitive compensation and benefits, including health insurance, and professional development opportunities.
Apply

27356.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor People, Training (Electrical Compliance), you will play a pivotal role in strengthening workforce capability by ensuring training programs meet regulatory requirements and operational needs.
You will directly contribute to a safe and compliant work environment by embedding robust electrical competency frameworks, supporting workforce development, and enabling teams to perform critical tasks safely and efficiently. Your work will have a lasting impact on both operational performance and the development of our people.
As part of our team, you will
Design, deliver, and continuously improve electrical training programs aligned with Newmont, industry, and HSE standards, ensuring compliance across all electrical work activities.
Deliver mandatory training and inductions, including Electrical Worker Inductions, High Voltage compliance, Arc Flash, Hazard Awareness, and Low Voltage Rescue.
Develop and maintain engaging training materials, competency frameworks, and verification processes to support both theoretical and on-the-job learning.
Provide hands-on training, coaching, and assessment for electrical workers, including High Voltage Operator training and assessment.
Maintain electrical competencies and worker authorisations within the Learning Management System (LMS), ensuring compliance and audit readiness.
Partner closely with Supervisors, Superintendents, Electrical Engineering, and HSE teams to align training with operational requirements, risk controls, and business needs.
Conduct field observations and training needs analysis to identify capability gaps and refine training programs.
Incorporate learnings from audits, incidents, and workforce feedback into training programs to drive continuous improvement.
Foster a collaborative learning environment that supports knowledge sharing and capability development.
Manage training resources effectively while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Demonstrated experience within fixed plant, processing, or resource sector environments (mining, oil, or gas preferred).
Electrical trade qualification, with instrumentation experience considered advantageous.
Certificate IV in Training and Assessment (or equivalent formal training qualification).
A current PNG Electrical License (NEA License).
Strong understanding of electrical compliance frameworks, competency-based training, and regulatory requirements.
High Voltage Switching Operations experience or qualifications, with relevant safety certifications highly regarded (e.g. First Aid, CPR, LV Rescue),
Experience developing and delivering training programs, including on-the-job training (OJT).
Understanding of training standards and industry requirements, with the ability to develop simple and clear learning materials.
Sound knowledge of permit systems, isolations, and operational safety practices.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Learning Management Systems, with the ability to manage training data and compliance records.
Sound understanding of adult learning principles and VET frameworks.
Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to work independently and prioritise effectively.
Well-developed stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence across all levels.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to work well with teams, coach others, and build positive working relationships.
Able to work independently, stay organised, and manage time effectively.
Your work environment
This role is based at Lihir Operations, working within a fast-paced and highly collaborative environment. You will engage closely with operations, maintenance teams, and leadership to support workforce development and compliance outcomes.
You will work alongside a diverse range of stakeholders, including training teams, site leadership, contractors, and external agencies, contributing to a culture of safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 (day shift) Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be part of a global organisation committed to safe, responsible, and sustainable mining. We are dedicated to developing our people and creating meaningful opportunities for career growth.
By joining our team, you will benefit from:
Exposure to world-class mining operations.
Opportunities for career development and progression into future leadership roles.
A strong safety culture where your contribution makes a difference every day.
A collaborative and inclusive workplace where your expertise is valued.
The opportunity to influence workforce capability and contribute to operational excellence.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number
43266
before the advertised closing date:
23 June 2026.
Apply

Understanding of different culture, community and or environment issues.
Communication proficiency
Problem solving and analysis.

27353.description:
Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Communications Lead
CARE International in PNG is recruiting a Communications Lead role based in Port Moresby. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
CARE International in Papua New Guinea (PNG) has a focus on Gender Equality, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Peace Building, Agriculture and Health.
CARE, along with Palladium, is positioning for an upcoming Asia Development Bank (ADB)-funded program: Sustainable Highlands Region Core Road Network Project (SHRCRNP) in Papua New Guinea; Strengthening and Diversifying Climate Resilient Livelihoods Program, which aims to improve livelihoods and resilience in Papua New Guinea’s highlands through climate-smart agriculture, inclusive value chains, and strengthened community infrastructure.
The project focuses on boosting agricultural productivity and market access, enhancing rural connectivity, and building local capacity to manage climate and environmental risks, with a strong emphasis on inclusion, sustainability, and partnerships with government and the private sector. It will operate primarily across the Highlands region, with activities concentrated in the Eastern Highlands, Western Highlands, Jiwaka, Simbu, and Enga provinces. The program is scheduled to run for four years, with EOIs currently under assessment.
This Position will have direct contact with Children or vulnerable adults.
The employee must demonstrate full compliance with all CARE policies and procedures.
This role is based in Port Moresby but will require travel to CARE PNG’s field offices and project sites as and when required.
SELECTION CRITERIA
A relevant qualification, minimum Bachelors level, in international development, community development, monitoring and evaluation, or strategic communications
Minimum 3 years of relevant experience; in community-based M&E. (COMPULSORY).
Experience in developing sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated indicators and monitoring inclusion outcomes(COMPULSORY).
Demonstrated experience in international development; strong understanding of international development theory and practice; and knowledge of key institutional (including ADB) donor priorities.
Demonstrated experience in the design and development of a range of internal and external communications products for livelihoods and/or women’s empowerment programs
Demonstrated understanding of gender equality and women’s empowerment and a commitment to CARE’s approach and values including ethnic diversity and cultural sensitivity.
Demonstrated high level of communication and interpersonal skills including the ability to create and foster collaborative and productive relationships, internally and externally
Demonstrated ability to liaise effectively with staff and stakeholders both verbally and in writing
Exceptional interpersonal skills including the ability to work independently and as amember of a cross-functional team. Includes the capacity to manage and support a small team.

Finance Manager
About Christian Leaders Training College (CLTC)
Christian Leaders’ Training College (CLTC) is a leading interdenominational Christian higher education institution dedicated to equipping Christian leaders for service throughout Papua New Guinea and the South Pacific. Located at Banz in Western Highlands Province, CLTC has been serving churches and communities for decades through quality theological education, leadership development, and community transformation initiatives. Guided by Christian values and a commitment to excellence, CLTC seeks dedicated professionals who are passionate about stewardship, integrity, and service.
Career Opportunity
Christian Leaders Training College (CLTC) is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified, experienced, and highly motivated individual to fill the position of Finance Manager. Reporting directly to the Vice Principal - Operations, the successful candidate will provide strategic financial leadership and ensure the effective management of the College’s financial resources, systems, and compliance obligations.
Key Accountabilities:
Lead and manage the overall financial operations of the College.
Develop, implement, and monitor annual budgets and financial plans.
Prepare timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports.
Ensure compliance with statutory, taxation, audit, and regulatory requirements.
Manage cash flow, financial forecasting, and banking functions.
Oversee payroll administration and financial controls.
Coordinate annual audits and liaise with external auditors and relevant stakeholders.
Monitor financial performance and provide strategic advice to the College leadership.
Develop and maintain sound financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Supervise and mentor finance staff to ensure high performance and professional development.
Support resource mobilization initiatives, grants management, and donor reporting requirements where applicable.
Promote accountability, transparency, and stewardship of College resources.
Key Requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
Professional accounting qualification (CPA, CA, or equivalent) will be highly regarded.
Minimum of five (5) years' experience in a senior finance or accounting role.
Demonstrated experience in financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and financial management.
Strong knowledge of accounting standards, taxation, and statutory compliance requirements.
Experience in managing audits and maintaining effective internal controls.
Proficiency in accounting and payroll software and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience within the education, church, non-government, or not-for-profit sector will be an advantage.
Key Attributes:
Strong Christian faith and commitment to Christian values and principles.
High level of integrity, honesty, and professionalism.
Proven leadership and team management capabilities.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.
Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy and accountability.

Self-motivated, proactive, and results-oriented.
Commitment to excellence, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

27338.description:
Mechanic
SPECTRA POM IS HIRING!
Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking organized and well experienced individuals to join our POM Workshop Team and be a part of our growing enterprise!
Position Description
Position Title: Mechanic
Company: Spectra Industrial
Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Reports To: Operations Manager / Southern Region Manager
Position Purpose
The Mechanic is responsible for inspecting, servicing, diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining company vehicles, plant, and equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation. The role requires a recognized mechanical trade qualification, practical workshop experience, compliance with Papua New Guinea workplace safety requirements, and the ability to complete maintenance records accurately.
Key Responsibilities
Inspection, Servicing & Preventive Maintenance
Carry out routine inspections, servicing, lubrication, and preventive maintenance on vehicles, plant, and equipment.
Perform pre-start, scheduled, and breakdown maintenance in line with workshop procedures and client standards.
Identify worn or damaged parts and recommend timely repair or replacement.
Fault Diagnosis & Repairs
Diagnose mechanical faults on engines, driveline, brakes, steering, suspension, and basic electrical systems.
Repair, overhaul, or replace defective parts and components using correct tools and workshop practices.
Test equipment after repair to confirm safe and reliable operating condition.
Workshop Tools, Parts & Equipment Care
Use workshop tools, testing equipment, and manuals correctly and safely.
Maintain tools and workshop equipment in good condition and report defects promptly.
Assist with ordering, collection, and proper use of spare parts, lubricants, and consumables.
Safety, Compliance & Housekeeping
Comply with company safety procedures, PPE requirements, toolbox talks, and Papua New Guinea workplace safety standards.
Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free workshop and work area.
Report hazards, incidents, unsafe equipment, and non-conformances promptly to the supervisor.
Documentation & Reporting
Complete job cards, service reports, inspection checklists, and maintenance records accurately and on time.
Record parts used, work completed, and outstanding repairs clearly for workshop tracking.
Communicate equipment status, defects, and maintenance priorities to supervisors and relevant teams.
Teamwork & Operational Support
Work closely with drivers, operators, stores, and workshop staff to meet operational requirements.
Assist apprentices or junior staff with on-the-job guidance where required.
Undertake additional duties, training, or site support as reasonably directed by management.
Breakdown & Field Support
Respond to workshop or field breakdowns and carry out repairs efficiently to minimize downtime.
Support site-based maintenance activities where travel or roster work is required.
Ensure repaired vehicles and equipment are safe, roadworthy, and ready for operation.
Key Competencies & Skills
Mechanical aptitude and diagnostic ability.
Safety awareness and compliance.
Attention to detail and workmanship.
Communication and reporting skills.
Teamwork, reliability, and initiative.
Ability to work under pressure and meet operational deadlines.
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Grade 10 education, Grade 12 is an advantage.
Recognized Mechanical Tradesman Certificate in Automotive or Motor Vehicle Mechanics from a recognized institution or NATTB-certified trade qualification.
Minimum 3–5 years’ relevant mechanic experience in a workshop, fleet, plant, construction, mining, oil and gas, or industrial environment.
Sound knowledge of preventive maintenance, fault diagnosis, repair procedures, and safe work practices.
Experience working on light vehicles, diesel equipment, plant, or heavy equipment is highly desirable.
Current PNG driver’s license, preferably Class 6, is required or highly advantageous depending on operational needs.
Ability to read service manuals, complete workshop documentation, and work independently or as part of a team.

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our exploration team, the primary purpose of this role is to ensure the operations of helicopter is in line with contractual requirements and also monitor and reduce costs associated explorations surface operations.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Oversee that the helicopters flight schedules and daily operations with contractors and K92 employees are in line with K92 processes and procedures.
Develop and maintain a cost control system for the exploration project, including cost tracking, forecasting, and reporting.
Work with the Exploration Manager to develop and monitor helicopter budgets and project budgets, ensuring that all expenditures are within budget limits and approved scope.
Develop and maintain a cost estimate database to support future exploration projects.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a strong character who is prepared to make hard decisions and deliver results. In addition to this, you will have the following.
Exceptional financial/logical skills with proficiency in MS Suite
Prior experience in accounting base packages such as Pronto
Ability to manage personnel and work effectively with diverse team.
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to make quick decisions under pressure.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

27384.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
Mechanical Technician supports safe and efficient power and utilities operations by executing inspections, repairs, and maintenance activities on mechanical equipment, ensuring asset reliability, compliance, and continuous plant availability.
Essential Duties
Perform routine inspections of plant and equipment
Identify and report defects early
Assist with breakdown repairs
Carry out repairs, adjustments, and part replacements
Support system testing and calibration
Ensure equipment reliability and performance standards
Maintain and update maintenance records and logs
Contribute to maintenance planning
Track and manage critical spare parts
Assist with inventory and parts availability
Follow all safety procedures and practices
Participate in safety initiatives and meetings
Identify recurring issues and suggest improvements
Help improve maintenance efficiency and reliability
Support a zero-harm safety culture
Training & Experience
Mechanical Trade Certificate (e.g., Fitter, Diesel Fitter, Mechanical Technician) or equivalentrecognized qualification
Completion of apprenticeship or formal trade training program
Demonstrated experience in mechanical maintenance within mining, processing, powergeneration, or heavy industrial environments
Experience with rotating and static plant equipment (e.g., pumps, engines, compressors,conveyors, or utility systems) (contextual application aligned to P&U)
Proven exposure to breakdown maintenance, fault finding, and preventive maintenanceactivities
Ability to interpret mechanical drawings, manuals, and maintenance procedures
Competence in using maintenance tools and equipment safely and effectively
Basic understanding of condition monitoring and defect identification
Experience with maintenance management systems (e.g., SAP/CMMS) for work order execution and history recording
Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices and adherence to site procedures
Experience in power and utilities systems (diesel generation, water, steam, or fuel systems)
Exposure to reliability maintenance and condition monitoring programs
High-risk work licenses (rigging, confined space, working at heights – if applicable to role)
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. 27363.description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Welder is responsible for performing specialized welding, fabrication, and structural repair tasks on Express Freight Management’s heavy-duty vehicle fleet (trucks, trailers), Material Handling Equipment (MHE), workshop fixtures, and general property assets. This role requires expertise in various welding techniques to ensure the structural integrity, safety, and longevity of the company’s equipment and assets.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Welding and Fabrication:
o Perform high-quality welding across various processes, including but not limited to
MIG (GMAW), TIG (GTAW), and Stick (SMAW)
, primarily on steel and aluminum used in heavy-duty applications.
o Execute custom fabrication and assembly of structural components, brackets, chassis reinforcements, and safety cages as required by the workshop or logistics operations.
o Repair cracks, breaks, and wear on heavy-duty vehicle chassis, trailer bodies, suspension points, roll-off containers, and MHE frames.
Repair and Maintenance:
o Conduct repairs on workshop infrastructure, racking systems, loading bay doors, and general metalwork within company properties.
o Cut, shape, and smooth materials using plasma cutters, grinders, torches, and other specialized tools.
o Liaise with mechanics and auto electricians to determine the scope of structural repairs needed for vehicles following damage or failure.
SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Skills

Welding Proficiency:
Expert-level skill in multiple welding processes (MIG and Stick essential; TIG highly desirable) and experience working with thick gauge metals common in heavy-duty commercial transport.

Fabrication Skills:
Strong ability to measure, cut, and assemble materials accurately and efficiently.

Blueprint Interpretation:
Proficient in reading and translating technical drawings, schematics, and welding symbols into finished products.

Safety Awareness:
Deep understanding of welding hazards and the strict application of safety protocols.

Attention to Detail:
Meticulous approach to quality control to ensure structural integrity and a professional finish on all repairs.
Qualifications
 Recognized Trade Qualification/Certification as a
Welder
(or equivalent).
 Minimum of
3-5 years of post-qualification experience
in a heavy industrial, truck/trailer repair, or construction environment.
How to Apply
If you meet the above criteria and are ready to contribute to a leading freight and logistics provider, please submit your CV and a cover letter to:
[email protected]
and
[email protected]
.

27333.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Trainer and Assessor (Processing Plant), you will play a critical role in building capability across our Process Plant Operations teams. You will design and deliver training programs that strengthen technical expertise, improve safety outcomes, and enable operational workforce to perform at their best.
Through coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job development, you will directly contribute to improving plant performance while ensuring work is carried out safely and efficiently.
As part of our team, you will
Develop and deliver training programs aligned to Newmont, industry, and HSE standards across process plant operations, ensuring all training materials are fit-for-purpose and compliant.
Provide hands-on, field-based training and coaching to operators across milling, grinding, flotation, and plant systems, delivering both theoretical and on-the-job learning in line with agreed training plans and progression pathways.
Mentor and support employees, including apprentices, operators, and supervisors, through continuous coaching and development, fostering capability growth and supporting succession planning into leadership roles.
Conduct training needs analysis in collaboration with operational leaders, updating priorities and aligning training plans to address identified capability gaps and business needs.
Engage closely with Supervisors, Superintendents, and Operations teams to ensure clear communication of training plans, schedules, and outcomes, maintaining strong alignment between Operations and Training.
Carry out field observations and actively assess workforce capability, using insights to refine and enhance training programs to ensure employees are fully developed and able to contribute to safe and efficient production.
Promote a culture of learning, collaboration, and continuous improvement by creating opportunities for employees to share knowledge and learn from each other.
Drive safe and productive behaviours through visible leadership, particularly within apprentice and trainee groups, influencing a strong safety-first culture.
Maintain accurate training records within the Learning Management System (LMS), monitor progress, and communicate results and feedback to participants and stakeholders.
Manage training resources effectively, including preparing requests for equipment and materials, while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Demonstrated experience within a complex processing or plant operations environment, ideally with experience in a hydrometallurgical processing plant.
Strong technical knowledge across process operations, including full circuit exposure (front end, back end, milling, grinding and flotation), with sound subject matter expertise.
Mining experience is advantageous, with a collaborative and confident approach when engaging with both frontline teams and leadership stakeholders.
Relevant training and assessment qualification (e.g. Certificate III/IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent), with experience in developing training materials, curricula, and delivering structured learning programs.
Well-developed facilitation, presentation, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage, coach, and influence individuals and groups across all levels of the organisation.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and learning systems, with the ability to manage training data, maintain records, and utilise learning databases effectively.
Strong technical writing and documentation skills, with the ability to interpret and customise standards (e.g. NATTB) into practical training materials, and audit compliance against those standards.
Sound understanding of adult learning principles, including individual and group training methodologies, and experience applying these in operational environments.
Knowledge of VET frameworks and processes, with the ability to align training outcomes to recognised standards and certification pathways.
Your work environment
This role is based at Lihir Operations, within a fast-paced and highly collaborative environment. You will work closely with Operations, Training, Health & Safety, and broader stakeholder groups to support workforce capability.
The position involves significant time in the field, delivering practical, hands-on training and engaging directly with teams to support real-time learning and development outcomes.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21- day shift, Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be part of an organisation committed to developing people, strengthening local capability, and creating meaningful career pathways.
Contribute directly to workforce capability, safety, and operational performance.
Play a key role in delivering new training programs and qualifications within PNG.
Access opportunities for career growth into leadership and specialist roles.
Work in an environment that values collaboration, continuous improvement, and learning.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number
43035
before the advertised closing date:
22 June 2026.
Apply

Job Scope
The Group Accounting Officer has a delegated responsibility for keeping the Kenmore Group subsidiary files in good financial and legal standing in assisting the Group Accountant with the consolidation of Financial Statements and Tax Compliance.
Key Responsibilities
Assist the Group Accountant in preparing consolidated financial statements, group debtors’ reports, and tax returns including GST, BIPT, SWT, and other statutory filings.
Liaise with the IRC regarding tax filing, payments, and reconciliations.
Coordinating with Kenmore subsidiaries Financial Controllers to obtain various reports for consolidation and other information required by the Group Accountant.
Monitor and maintain records of CAPEX (Capital Expenditure) requisitions and related filings.
Ensure compliance with accounting standards, IRC rules and regulations, and company audit obligations.
Filing and assisting on other jobs as and when required by the Group Accountant.
Qualifications and Experience
A Diploma or Degree in Business or Accounting is essential
12 months or more experience in the said tax environment in a large scale corporate environment, is essential.
Self-driven, results oriented and analytical.
A genuine passion for the financial field and industry.
Willing to take on new challenges as part of professional growth and development.
Excellent personal credibility, interpersonal skills and self confidence in dealing with Staff and Management at all levels.
About Us
The Head Office of the Kenmore Group of Companies is located at Ela Beach Tower, Bramel Street, Port Moresby where the Group’s Finance, Information Communication & Technology and Corporate Support and Compliance Department provide business support services to our subsidiary branches through-out PNG.
In recognition of your contribution, we in turn provide on-the-job training as well as soft skill training at the Kenmore Training Centre to advance your workplace professional development. A competitive remuneration package will be offered, commensurate to qualifications and experience.

Commencement: July 2026
Long term role, up to June 2027(w/potential for extension)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to Papua New Guinea citizens only
*Abt is committed to advancing women’s leadership in PNG’s economic development and are building an environment where women can lead progress and shape economic outcomes. Abt promotes an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment for women and encourages PNG women and men to apply.
This position includes health insurance and supportive workplace for parents and carers, including relevant leave and other benefits.
About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
APEP supports the PNGRGC which is an umbrella organisation for civil society organisations (CSOs) with an interest in the extractives sector, including community-based, faith-based, legal, environmental, transparency and anticorruption organisations.  The mission of the PNGRGC is to raise public awareness on resource governance and sustainability issues – and specifically to advocate for accountability and good governance in the planning and management of the extractive sector, including resource allocation and licensing, development options and community participation, and safeguarding of PNG’s national heritage consistent with the National Constitution. The PNGRGC is also mandated to coordinate civil society’s participation in PNG Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (PNGEITI), including providing guidance and support to the CSO representatives on the PNGEITI Multi Stakeholder Group (MSG).
About the Opportunity
The PNGRGC Operations Manager will effectively function as the Executive Officer of the two-person secretariat of the PNGRGC. This role will require the coordination and management of the logistics and administration activities within the PNGRGC office and plays a lead role in implementing the PNGRGC operations plan.
The Operations Manager will take the lead in drafting high quality reporting and manage PNGRGC coordination with key stakeholders and will also have the primary responsibility for ensuring the effective and efficient delivery of the PNGRGC objectives.
Key responsibilities
The PNGRGC Operations Manager is responsible for ensuring the efficient operations of the PNGRGC. The primary responsibilities include facilitating the building of organisational capacity and membership, communication and networking; advocacy; and fundraising. The core responsibilities of this position are but not limited to.
Undertake monitoring and evaluation of engagements among stakeholders.
Ensure programme work plans and timelines are regularly monitored to ensure timely delivery of milestones.
Ensure that all reporting is delivered in a timely manner and in accordance with the PNGRGC constitutional requirements and deadlines.
Ensure APEP objectives are upheld including coordinating GEDSI activities and communication priorities.
Ensure the business of PNGRGC operates with the highest standards of conduct and ethics and maintain the reputation for quality and excellence.
Provide an effective and timely tracking of deliverables, milestones, risks and program progress as well as effective, accurate and regular updates to PNGRGC Council and APEP.
Provide executive support to PNGRGC Secretariat’s office and the Council.

Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Boilermaker
to join our Fixed Plant Maintenance team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Fabrication Supervisor, the primary responsibility of the Boilermaker is to provide support in maintenance of Fixed Plant Equipment (as designated), while ensuring health, safety, environmental, community relations and quality workmanship standards are maintained, all for the best value. Undertaking work to maintenance/repair schedule.

Undertaking & carrying out other operational tasks as required.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values

Strong communication skills and the ability to effectively manage time

Prepared to accept responsibility

27311.description:
High autonomy and visibility across the full project lifecycle.
Shape PNG's energy future through transformative projects.
Work across power generation, transmission and distribution projects.
Lead transformational energy projects that power industries, connect communities, and shape Papua New Guinea's future.
Peopleconnexion is partnering with a nationally owned independent power producer and developer delivering critical energy infrastructure across Papua New Guinea. With an expanding portfolio spanning power generation, transmission and distribution networks, substations, industrial power supply projects, and renewable mini-grid developments, our client is at the forefront of providing reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions across both urban and remote communities.
This is an opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of high-impact projects, including:
Power generation and transmission developments
Transmission and distribution infrastructure projects
Industrial power supply and network expansion initiatives
Renewable energy and rural electrification projects
Remote community mini-grid developments
This is a unique opportunity to play a leading role in nation-building infrastructure projects, with visibility across the entire project lifecycle and the ability to influence outcomes from concept and feasibility through to commissioning and handover.
The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced
Project Manager – Power, Infrastructure & Rural Electrification
to take ownership of the beginning-to-end delivery of complex energy and infrastructure projects. This is a senior leadership position requiring a technically grounded professional with strong commercial acumen, stakeholder management capability, and the ability to successfully deliver projects in dynamic and often remote operating environments.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the full project lifecycle from feasibility, concept development and design through to procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover
Manage feasibility studies, concept design activities, and project development initiatives
Develop and manage project schedules, budgets, financial models, and risk management frameworks
Provide CAPEX and OPEX cost inputs to support business cases and financial modelling
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations
Manage contractors, consultants, suppliers, and vendors, including tendering, contract negotiation, performance management, and commercial oversight
Drive project governance through reporting, progress tracking, cost control, risk management, and stakeholder communication
Ensure compliance with HSE, regulatory, environmental, and quality standards throughout all phases of project delivery
Manage stakeholder relationships across internal teams, government agencies, utilities, regulators, landowner groups, and local communities
Monitor project performance, manage variations, and deliver projects safely, on time, and within budget.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
10+ years' experience in project management within the power, energy, utilities, or large-scale infrastructure sectors
Demonstrated experience delivering generation, transmission, distribution, renewable energy, or rural electrification projects from concept through to commissioning
Strong commercial capability across budgeting, financial management, cost control, procurement, and contract administration
Proven leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams and complex contractor environments
Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence outcomes across technical, commercial, regulatory, and community interfaces
Experience working in remote, developing, or high-pressure environments with a high degree of resilience and adaptability
Tertiary qualifications in Engineering (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical, or related discipline) or a relevant technical field
A hands-on, solutions-focused approach with the ability to balance strategic thinking and operational delivery.
Why Join?
This is more than a project management role—it is an opportunity to contribute to critical infrastructure that directly impacts industries, businesses, and communities throughout Papua New Guinea.
You will join a growing organisation with a strong pipeline of power and infrastructure developments, offering exposure to both traditional and renewable energy projects, significant autonomy, and the opportunity to leave a lasting legacy through projects that improve connectivity, economic growth, and community electrification across the country.
If you are a delivery-focused Project Manager ready to take ownership of complex, high-value energy and infrastructure projects, we welcome a confidential discussion.
To apply, upload your CV and covering letter by clicking on the "APPLY NOW" button and register your interest for this role.
Applications Close: COB Thursday 18th June 2026

Security Coordinator
Job Summary:
Responsible for all security and safety programs, plans and policies relevant to the project including detailed security procedures that comply with security policies. This includes emergency response drills and communication procedures for the project.  May provide security coordination for the projects in response to incidents, emergencies, and crises on behalf of the project.  Execute exercises, simulations, and test cases which the country office or program staff prepare for contingencies. Supports and administers organizational security plans and operations. Executes   procedures and processes to provide physical protection for personnel and company property and meet required codes and regulations. Compiles data for loss control and accident reports.
Accountabilities:
Supports the Security Team to develop, manage, and coordinate organization-wide security programs to address a variety of needs and issues.
Interacts and coordinates with networks of security professionals and vendors to help safeguard the organization’s personnel, assets, and intellectual property.
Prepares risk and threat assessment reports and mitigation recommendations for internal use.
Participates in field assessments of new project implementation areas; documents the results using FHI 360 standard templates.
Helps develop and establish the Country Security Plan and other security policies and procedures.
Conducts security and political risk analyses.
Conducts security/risk management training for staff.
Following humanitarian principles, develops relationships with relevant authorities and community leaders to ensure access for ongoing programming.
Interfaces with all levels of staff across functional areas to include Procurement, ISS, Human Resources, and Contracts and Grants.

K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. Perform roadworks and manage spillage and sump bogging
Maintain high standards of work quality and safety compliance
Identify and escalate opportunities for operational efficiency

Ability to work with close supervision.
Must have Underground Mining experience.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
